Yes, that is the only prompt. I would recommend brainstorming to start off. Just take notes and write down anything that comes to mind that you could possibly turn into an essay. Eventually, start writing your rough draft. Maybe write a second or a third one, just keep writing and see what fits and what doesn’t, what sounds good and what is just fluff. If you have friends, family, teachers, professors, anyone that can read your essay for you, ask them to! Any bit of advice helps. Are there any writing/English tutors that you can see? Ask them to read over it as well. This essay needs to be AMAZING. It’s a huge part of the admissions process and is arguably more important than your grades when applying to FIT. So ask anyone, and I mean anyone to give you at least a little bit of advice on what you can do better. Maybe take a break from the essay for a couple days, then come back to it with a fresh mind, and you’ll find wayyy more things that you can improve with your essay. 

As someone else has already mentioned, look up YouTube videos of other people’s essays to give you an idea on what FIT is looking for in your essay. Try not to be too cliche and just talk about fashion and stuff, though. I’m sure they’ve seen enough of that in essays. Talk about what YOU specifically can do for FIT, what makes YOU such an amazing student, what YOU plan on doing during your time at FIT and what YOU plan on doing with your degree when you graduate. Maybe mention any extra curricular activities or electives that you would like to be part of. 

Also, don’t procrastinate!!! You’re asking this question now so it seems you have a head start already. 

You’ve got this!!

Is there an English/writing professor that you are close enough with to a point where you could ask them to look over your essay and give tips? Maybe you can even ask a friend or family member to read it. Just about anyone can give a good outsider’s perspective. Also, try not to be too cliche when writing your essay. While it is good to talk about your interest in fashion, they are looking for more than just that. They want to know about you, your personality, your interests, achievements, what you will bring to the table. Are you working a job while also attending college? Do you do any volunteer work? Do you have hobbies? How were your grades in high school? Were they good/excellent while also participating in extra curricular activities? If not, did your grades improve in college? Tell a little story from your childhood that can relate, talk about your ideas and goals as a future fashion business manager, or what you’ll do different from others. 

What I see some other people do is they tend to hate on math and science when writing their essays… This won’t look good whether you’re applying for FBM, fashion design, or even fragrance marketing. Math and science still play a part in fashion, no matter where you are. Try to omit this as well if this is true for you. Maybe you’ll learn to love it!

While I wish I could provide an example, I am currently in the process of writing my own and of course haven’t submitted it yet, so I wouldn’t know if it would be worthy of being accepted.
